name: Water

sections.body: Vanilla RimWorld treats thirst as background texture. Sands of Arrakis makes it the first planning problem. Water is now a colony-wide logistics loop with consequences for labor, travel, heat management, clothing, and settlement layout.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Colonists spawn into a world where hydration is always running down. The meter begins high, but not safely high, which means a new settlement starts under pressure rather than comfort. That establishes the tone of Arrakis from the first morning.
sections.title: Water need

sections.body: Thirst is not constant. Hotter ambient bands and unroofed exposure accelerate loss, so the same stockpile of rations can feel generous indoors and suddenly inadequate once work shifts move onto open sand.
sections.title: Heat and exposure

sections.body: Stillsuits, reclamation masks, and headwraps are the player-facing answer to attrition. The system is intentionally generous enough to feel meaningful and intentionally capped so the player still respects water as a resource instead of solving it forever.
sections.title: Water retention

sections.body: The colony survives by turning atmosphere, time, and careful siting into sealed rations. Windtraps and portable condensers make water visible as infrastructure, while cisterns and hauling keep the network from collapsing under distance.
sections.title: Collectors and storage

summary: Water is the central survival law of the mod. Heat, exposure, stillsuit discipline, storage, and collection all decide whether a colony merely works or actually endures.
